items.title: Add strong contact shadows so fighters don’t look pasted on
items.what: Gameplay screens (e.g., the full-fight view with both sticks visible): both fighters’ feet sit on the tatami with essentially no contact shadow/occlusion directly under the soles—especially noticeable under the white gi fighter’s front foot and the red gi fighter’s lead foot, which read like they’re floating a few pixels above the floor.
items.why: This is an immediate “cheap compositing” tell in the first seconds of play; it breaks depth, reduces impact of strikes, and undermines the otherwise cinematic dojo lighting.
items.how: Add a dedicated blob/contact shadow per fighter (elliptical dark decal) anchored to each foot or averaged between feet; fade/scale it with stance width and vertical motion (jump/crouch). If sprites can’t receive 3D shadows, render a soft plane-projected shadow pass or draw a 2D shadow quad in world space under each fighter with a multiply blend and slight blur.

items.title: Increase contrast of the twin-stick HUD and its labels
items.what: Bottom third of gameplay screens: the stick rings, arrows, and especially the labels “STANCE” / “TECHNIQUE” and the micro-instructions inside the circles (“MOVE & JUMP”, “STRIKE”, step/jump/crouch, etc.) are so low-contrast they nearly disappear into the vignette (they’re only faintly visible even on the brighter tatami).
items.why: On a phone, players need to understand controls instantly; low-contrast UI reads as “non-interactive decoration,” causing early confusion and missed inputs.
items.how: Bump UI luminance/alpha for control strokes and text (e.g., +30–50%); add a subtle dark backing plate behind each stick (a soft radial gradient at ~30–40% opacity) to decouple it from the background; increase label size/weight by one step and apply a 1–2px shadow/outline for legibility.

items.title: Make the boot/loading progress unmistakable
items.what: ShoeMoney pre-boot screen: “Starting up · 0%” is tiny and very dim at center-lower, and the progress bar is a hairline stroke near the bottom edge with almost no fill/contrast—easy to miss against the dark background.
items.why: If loading feedback is unclear, players assume the game is frozen and bounce (especially in a browser).
items.how: Increase the percent text size and brightness (and/or move it closer to the bar); thicken the bar (min 6–8px), raise contrast between track and fill, and add a subtle animated shimmer/pulse so motion communicates “working” even at 0–1%.

items.title: Reduce the oversized title block so the fight and fighters read first
items.what: Pre-fight “QUALIFIER vs HasanAbi” screen: the word “QUALIFIER” dominates the upper half, while the fighters sit relatively small in the middle with a lot of unused negative space above them; the primary action CTA (“FIGHT · 2”) competes with the huge headline rather than being the clear focal point.
items.why: Players come for the bout; over-weighting the header delays comprehension of what to do next and makes the scene feel less punchy on a small portrait screen.
items.how: Scale the “QUALIFIER” headline down ~20–30% (or move it up into the top HUD strip), tighten vertical spacing, and enlarge/raise the fighters slightly so their faces/hands sit closer to mid-screen. Keep the CTA as the largest interactive element in the lower third and ensure it’s visually separated from the dimmed stick graphics behind it.

items.title: Fix small hit targets and faint state indicators in Moves/Settings overlays
items.what: Techniques and Settings overlays: the close “X” in the top-right is small relative to the screen and near the edge; in Settings, the checkboxes are thin-outline empty squares with no strong state mark (and low contrast against the dark panel), making toggles hard to parse at a glance.
items.why: On touch, small/edge-adjacent targets cause mis-taps; unclear toggle state creates mistrust (“did that setting actually turn on?”).
items.how: Increase tap target sizes to at least ~44px (even if the icon stays smaller) with more inset from the screen edge; make checkbox states unambiguous (filled box + checkmark, or on/off pill switches). Raise contrast of secondary text (e.g., the small explanatory lines) by one step and ensure consistent divider/row spacing for scanability.
